Deep within me—below the diaphragm—something savage stirred.

Something waking. Something moving.
Something planted in me that day.

I imagined an impossible womb.
I sensed an impossible unborn creature.

Monster. That was its name.
The imagined thing seemed to be coming into the world, and the pain was terrible. But no monster existed. No such event was taking place in my body. Even that was delusion. Only the pain was real.

Ryoubu Suzukawa. Shinkai. Neither possessed this impossible source of an impossible creature. No one could see it. No one could touch it. An entire happening without an actual thing happening. Pure delusion.

And yet—this alone.
This enormous, overflowing strength was real!

Even at my call, the armor did not move. It sent only quiet words.

Death was coming. The strongest and most terrible, the demon armor sung of as destroying all who came near, was about to release the ultimate of its curse. An absolutely unavoidable fate of death. Muramasa.

I knew it. I understood it. Shinkai's steel—the wall that was meant to be matchless and invincible—could never stop the thing that was about to arrive.

At last I realized why a demon armor is a demon armor. That was death. That was ruin. Only pure, simple that.

I should not have got involved. I should not have come near.
